title: Saugust Neck (Southold Old Field)
summary: Saugust is recorded as a neck of land at the east part of Southold.
history_content: A 1662 Southold record described about thirty acres in Saugust neck. The name was probably transferred by settlers familiar with Saugus or Saugust at Lynn, Massachusetts, rather than being the name of a local Native owner.
translation_content:
Saugust is connected with a root meaning an outlet of a river or brook, with a locative ending meaning at or near.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are neither neutral nor innocent, but are brimming with social, political, and cultural meaning and significance.”

— Francesco Perono Cacciafoco and Francesco Cavallaro, Synchronic Toponymy (2023), Chapter summary
preservation_content: Saugust shows how Native-language place-names could move with settlers and then attach to Long Island landscapes, while still carrying Algonquian geographic meaning.
